The '''''Daily News and Analysis''''', abbreviated as '''''DNA''''', is a [[Hindi]]-language news program on [[Zee News]] and former English-language newspaper in India. It was taken over by the [[Zee Media Corporation]] in 2012 and essentially shut down except for using its brand name for the news program.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.exchange4media.com/industry-briefing-news/zee-news-re-launches-its-prime-time-show-dna-129008.html |title=Zee News re-launches its primetime show ''DNA'' | work=Exchange4media | date=7 August 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231022103602/https://www.exchange4media.com/industry-briefing-news/zee-news-re-launches-its-prime-time-show-dna-129008.html |archive-date= 22 Oct 2023 }}</ref> ''DNA'' was first launched as a broadsheet newspaper out of [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]] on 30 July 2005<ref name="launch" /> through a 50:50 joint venture between the Zee Media Corporation and the [[Dainik Bhaskar]] group under the company name Diligent Media Corporation Ltd.<ref name="launch">{{Cite web|url=https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/...and-dna-sets-july-30-as-its-launch-dateunveils-final-leg-of-pre-launch-marketing-16971.html |title=...And DNA sets July 30 as its launch date; unveils final leg of pre-launch marketing. | work=Exchange4media|date=12 July 2005|access-date=26 July 2023 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230725192159/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/...and-dna-sets-july-30-as-its-launch-dateunveils-final-leg-of-pre-launch-marketing-16971.html |archive-date= 25 Jul 2023 }}</ref>

The newspaper had first launched its outdoor advertising campaign through billboards and placards in Mumbai during early 2005, with the tagline, "Speak Up, It's in Your DNA",<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.afaqs.com/news/advertising/21826_daily-news--analysis-outdoor-is-in-its-dna | title=Daily News and Analysis: Outdoor is in its DNA | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728082455/https://www.afaqs.com/news/advertising/21826_daily-news--analysis-outdoor-is-in-its-dna |archivedate=2023-07-28 | first=Devina | last=Joshi | work=afaqs! | date=5 August 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/dna-targets-august-15-launch-dateunveils-campaign-to-get-advance-bookings-16576.html | title=DNA targets August 15 launch date, unveils campaign to get advance bookings | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230728082458/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/dna-targets-august-15-launch-dateunveils-campaign-to-get-advance-bookings-16576.html |archivedate=2023-07-28 | publisher=exchange4media | date=14 June 2005}}</ref> which became its catch-phrase over the months. With the announcement of the launch of ''DNA'' came several other rival newspapers by large media conglomerates in the city, including the first-time-ever Mumbai edition of the predominantly north-Indian ''[[Hindustan Times]]''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.exchange4media.com/advertising-news/hindustan-times-to-launch-mumbai-edition-on-july-14-16969.html | title=Hindustan Times to Launch Mumbai Edition on July 14 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725192159/https://www.exchange4media.com/advertising-news/hindustan-times-to-launch-mumbai-edition-on-july-14-16969.html |archivedate=2023-07-25 | publisher=exchange4media | date=11 July 2005 | accessdate=26 July 2023}}</ref> and the ''[[Times of India]]''{{'}}s rival the ''[[Mumbai Mirror]]''<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/11535_battleground-mumbai-bombay-mirror-may-be-launched-by-may-30 | title=Battleground Mumbai: Bombay Mirror may be launched by May 30 | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726123807/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/11535_battleground-mumbai-bombay-mirror-may-be-launched-by-may-30 |archivedate=2023-07-26 | first=Viveat Susan | last=Pinto | work=afaqs! | date=24 May 2005}}</ref> newspaper that was later digitised into a web portal during the pandemic.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.newslaundry.com/2020/12/05/times-group-ceases-publication-of-pune-mirror-mumbai-mirror-to-relaunch-as-a-weekly | title=Times Group ceases publication of Pune Mirror, Mumbai Mirror to 'relaunch' as a weekly | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230801010508/https://www.newslaundry.com/2020/12/05/times-group-ceases-publication-of-pune-mirror-mumbai-mirror-to-relaunch-as-a-weekly |archivedate=2023-08-01 | publisher=Newslaundry | date=5 December 2020}}</ref>

The competition battleground between the three media conglomerates led to a massive spike in journalists' salaries in Bombay by almost 40–50 per cent of the earlier market rate, or even more, in the 3–4 months prior to the launches, as journalists began receiving hefty counter-offers from the opponent publication they were set to be joining.<ref name="antipoaching" />

It also saw a hike in salary of internal staff in TOI's [[Delhi]] office in order to ensure the editorial staff could be retained. Finally, the [[Times Group]] signed anti-poaching agreements or pacts with ''[[The Hindustan Times]]'' and ''[[The Telegraph India|The Telegraph]]'' of Calcutta in May 2005, in order to restrict themselves from hiring and poaching each other's staff.<ref name="antipoaching">[https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/times-group-signs-non-poaching-agreements-with-ht-and-telegraph-16366.html "Times Group signs non-poaching agreements with HT and Telegraph".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726153201/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/times-group-signs-non-poaching-agreements-with-ht-and-telegraph-16366.html |date=2023-07-26 }} ''exchange4media''. 30 May 2005.</ref>

== Coverage ==

''DNA'' catalysed several shifts in the Indian news media over the years. Its focus began with developing [[hyperlocal]] teams of reporters around Mumbai covering news from around the neighbouring municipal localities such as [[Thane]] and [[Vashi]]<ref name="forbes">[https://www.forbesindia.com/article/boardroom/dna-newspaper-attempts-mission-impossible/17632/1 "DNA Newspaper Attempts Mission Impossible".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725192202/https://www.forbesindia.com/article/boardroom/dna-newspaper-attempts-mission-impossible/17632/1 |date=2023-07-25 }} Rohin Dharmakumar. ''Forbes India''. 27 September 2010. Retrieved 26 July 2023.</ref> and the eastern and western suburbs of Mumbai as well as the iconic [[south Mumbai]] town area — through regional reporting bureaus managing the news coverage for ''DNA'''s local ''Zone'' and city pages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/india/is-dna-going-local-with-its-news-coverage-183167.html |title=Is DNA going local with its news coverage?| first=Anant |last=Rangaswami | work=[[Firstpost]]| date=16 January 2012 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726121754/https://www.firstpost.com/india/is-dna-going-local-with-its-news-coverage-183167.html |archive-date= 26 Jul 2023 }}</ref>

Over the years, the paper further expanded into local editions at Surat and Ahmedabad,<ref>[https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/dna-enters-gujarat-with-ahmedabad-and-surat-editions-28430.html "DNA enters Gujarat with Ahmedabad and Surat editions".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725195616/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/dna-enters-gujarat-with-ahmedabad-and-surat-editions-28430.html |date=2023-07-25 }} ''exchange4media''. 2 November 2007.</ref> then Pune,<ref>[https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/20171_dna-expands-to-pune-positions-paper-along-mumbai-lines "DNA expands to Pune, positions paper along Mumbai lines".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725195616/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/20171_dna-expands-to-pune-positions-paper-along-mumbai-lines |date=2023-07-25 }} ''afaqs!''. 17 January 2008.</ref> then Jaipur,<ref>[https://www.campaignindia.in/article/dna-launches-its-fifth-edition-in-jaipur-on-june-7/408592 "DNA launches its fifth edition in Jaipur on June 7".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726093919/https://www.campaignindia.in/article/dna-launches-its-fifth-edition-in-jaipur-on-june-7/408592 |date=2023-07-26 }} ''Campaign India''. 9 June 2008.</ref> then Bangalore,<ref>[https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/22930_dna-launches-its-bengaluru-edition "DNA launches its Bengalaru edition".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725194801/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/22930_dna-launches-its-bengaluru-edition |date=2023-07-25 }} Dhleta Surender Kumar. ''afaqs!''. 19 December 2008.</ref> then Indore,<ref>[https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/30945_dna-enters-mp-launches-indore-edition "DNA enters MP, launches Indore edition".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726121753/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/30945_dna-enters-mp-launches-indore-edition |date=2023-07-26 }} Sumantha Rathore. ''afaqs!''. 27 June 2011.</ref> and finally Delhi.<ref>[https://www.newslaundry.com/2016/10/04/dna-comes-to-delhi-finally "DNA comes to Delhi. Finally".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725195617/https://www.newslaundry.com/2016/10/04/dna-comes-to-delhi-finally |date=2023-07-25 }} Kaushik Chatterji. ''Newslaundry''. 4 October 2016.</ref>

Diligent Media Corporation Limited used to also bring out the business broadsheet newspaper ''DNA Money'' from [[Indore]], to cover business and finance, as a standalone sister newspaper to ''DNA'' during 2006,<ref>[https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/13861_dna-money-to-be-launched-as-a-stand-alone-newspaper "DNA Money to be launched as a stand-alone newspaper".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810230519/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/13861_dna-money-to-be-launched-as-a-stand-alone-newspaper |date=2023-08-10 }} Prajjal Saha. ''afaqs''. 11 January 2006.</ref> and it used to publish several women-centric and youth-centric lifestyle magazines as well,<ref>[https://www.campaignindia.in/article/dna-launches-the-mag-on-sunday/409733 "DNA launches The Mag on Sunday".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810225124/https://www.campaignindia.in/article/dna-launches-the-mag-on-sunday/409733 |date=2023-08-10 }} ''Campaign India''. 24 February 2009.</ref> such as ''DNA Ya!'', which was a supplement targeted at kids and young adults.<ref>[https://www.eventfaqs.com/news/ef-01593/dna-ya-organises-art-hunt-1279109583622 "DNA Ya! organises Art Hunt for children across 80 Schools in Mumbai".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022112343/https://www.eventfaqs.com/news/ef-01593/dna-ya-organises-art-hunt-1279109583622 |date=2023-10-22 }} ''eventfaqs''. 15 July 2010.</ref>

== Closure of print operations ==

The paper had begun to suffer tremendous losses over the years; it started shuttering its operations in Surat shortly after its launch,<ref name="forbes" /> and, by 2012, Zee had taken over the rest of the ownership of ''DNA'' from the Bhaskar group.<ref>[https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/dna-zee-close-to-buying-out-dainik-bhaskar-112040200008_1.html "DNA: Zee Close to Buying Out Dainik Bhaskar".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725192159/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/dna-zee-close-to-buying-out-dainik-bhaskar-112040200008_1.html |date=2023-07-25 }} Varada Bhat, Shubhashish, Surajeet Das Gupta. ''Business Standard''. First published 2 April 2012. Updated on 21 Jan 2013. Retrieved 26 July 2023.</ref><ref>[https://www.mxmindia.com/uncategorized/what-makes-zee-such-a-force-to-reckon-with/ "What makes Zee such a force to reckon with".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725193704/https://www.mxmindia.com/uncategorized/what-makes-zee-such-a-force-to-reckon-with/ |date=2023-07-25 }} Pradyuman Maheshwari. ''MxMIndia''. 1 October 2012. Retrieved 26 July 2023.</ref> It had also shut down its lifestyle magazine ''Me'' in 2010, citing that the paper's business was geared more towards news and that "the magazine business was dropping" as a whole.<ref>[https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/no-magazinesonly-newsdna-shuts-down-me-39055.html "No magazines, only news: DNA shuts down 'Me{{'"}}.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726150222/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-print-news/no-magazinesonly-newsdna-shuts-down-me-39055.html |date=2023-07-26 }} Akash Raha. ''exchange4media''. 11 August 2010.</ref>

By August 2014, the newspaper had also shut down its Bangalore and Pune editions<ref>[https://www.medianama.com/2014/08/223-dna-bangalore-pune/ "English Daily DNA Abruptly Shuts Its Bangalore & Pune Editions".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726113113/https://www.medianama.com/2014/08/223-dna-bangalore-pune/ |date=2023-07-26 }} Vikas SN. ''MediaNama''. 26 August 2014.</ref> and, in February 2019, it also closed the Jaipur and Delhi editions.<ref>[https://www.newslaundry.com/2019/10/09/the-medium-is-changing-not-us-dna-shuts-down-print-edition {{"'}}The medium is changing, not us': DNA shuts down print edition".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726103022/https://www.newslaundry.com/2019/10/09/the-medium-is-changing-not-us-dna-shuts-down-print-edition |date=2023-07-26 }} ''Newslaundry''. 9 October 2019.</ref> In October 2019, Zee Media Corporation announced that the entire newspaper (including the remaining editions in Ahmedabad and Mumbai) would be closed<ref>[https://theprint.in/india/dna-goes-out-of-print-14-years-after-launch-rise-fall-promising-newspaper/304050/ "DNA goes out of print 14 years after launch — the rise and sudden fall of a promising newspaper".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230501090335/https://theprint.in/india/dna-goes-out-of-print-14-years-after-launch-rise-fall-promising-newspaper/304050/ |date=2023-05-01 }} Amrita Nayak Datta. ''The Print''. 11 October 2019.</ref><ref>[https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/dna-publishes-its-last-print-edition-to-continue-as-web-portal "DNA publishes its last print edition, to continue as web portal".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725192159/https://www.afaqs.com/news/media/dna-publishes-its-last-print-edition-to-continue-as-web-portal |date=2023-07-25 }} 11 October 2019. ''afaqs!''.</ref> with the aim of optimizing costs and reducing the company's losses.<ref>[https://www.newslaundry.com/2019/06/12/dna-newspaper-slow-death-essel-group "How DNA newspaper is dying a slow and painful death".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725192200/https://www.newslaundry.com/2019/06/12/dna-newspaper-slow-death-essel-group |date=2023-07-25 }} Gaurav Sarkar. ''Newslaundry''. 12 June 2019. Retrieved 26 July 2023.</ref>

== TV show ==

[[Zee News]] continues to host ''DNA'' as a weekly news bulletin show, which is a prime-time [[Hindi-language]] programme hosted on the channel between 9.00 pm to 10.30 pm every weekday from Monday to Friday. The show had begun in 2012 with news anchor [[Sudhir Chaudhary (journalist)|Sudhir Chaudhary]] as its host, who had rejoined the channel in a second career stint. Chaudhary, who had launched the Sahara Samay channel for Sahara TV prior to this, had earlier also been with Zee till 2003.<ref>[https://www.exchange4media.com/media-tv-news/sudhir-chaudhary-moves-on-from-zee-news-after-a-decade-of-shaping-its-dna-121134.html "Sudhir Chaudhary moves on from Zee News after a decade of shaping its DNA".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230727175016/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-tv-news/sudhir-chaudhary-moves-on-from-zee-news-after-a-decade-of-shaping-its-dna-121134.html |date=2023-07-27 }} ''exchange4media''. 1 July 2022.</ref> Rohit Ranjan took over the DNA show in July 2022 after Chaudhary left to join {{lang|hi-latn|[[Aaj Tak]]|italic=no}}.<ref name="rohitsudhir">[https://www.exchange4media.com/media-tv-news/rohit-ranjan-returns-to-host-dna-on-zee-news-121429.html "Rohit Ranjan returns to host DNA on Zee News".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230727175015/https://www.exchange4media.com/media-tv-news/rohit-ranjan-returns-to-host-dna-on-zee-news-121429.html |date=2023-07-27 }} ''exchange4media''. 19 July 2022.</ref>

Chaudhary told ZMCL chairperson [[Subhash Chandra]] in his resignation letter that he was intending to use his fan following to start his own venture at some point,<ref>[https://brandequity.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/the-people-report/sudhir-chaudhary-resigns-as-ceo-of-zee-media/92632249 "Sudhir Chaudhary resigns as CEO of Zee Media".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230729085105/https://brandequity.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/the-people-report/sudhir-chaudhary-resigns-as-ceo-of-zee-media/92632249 |date=2023-07-29 }} ''The Economic Times''. 3 July 2022.</ref> while Chandra stated that he had attempted to persuade Chaudhary to stay back.<ref>"[https://www.newslaundry.com/2022/07/02/why-did-sudhir-chaudhary-leave-zee Why did Sudhir Chaudhary leave Zee?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230727175016/https://www.newslaundry.com/2022/07/02/why-did-sudhir-chaudhary-leave-zee |date=2023-07-27 }}" Tanishka Sodhi and Ashwine Kumar Singh. ''Newslaundry''. 2 July 2022.</ref>
